text.title: Contextual Inquiry Decision Tree
text.summary: Routes on whether real ongoing work in the real setting is reachable at all, what shape the booked session would actually take, and how the rows are being written up — to full field sessions, a session-design correction, an n=1 constraint, or a skip to interviews or telemetry.

decision-tree.root-question: What access to real, ongoing work can actually be obtained — and is the question one that observing work could answer?

branch.when: no live work setting is reachable, or the work is legally unobservable (clinical, classified, regulated customer data) and redaction would remove the content

conclusion.verdict: skip: without access to real work the method loses its only advantage over an interview while keeping its full cost — run a diary study or interviews and label them as such

branch.when: the question is comparative or quantitative — which label wins, what share of users do X — or the work is instantaneous and fully instrumented

conclusion.verdict: skip: contextual inquiry produces no rates; a benchmark test or the existing telemetry answers this at lower cost

branch.when: the product does not exist yet and there is no current analogue practice anyone performs

conclusion.verdict: skip: there is no work to sit beside — run generative interviews or concept work until an analogue practice exists to observe

branch.when: sessions can be booked where a participant does their own ongoing work
branch.question: What would the booked session actually look like on the day?

branch.when: a conference-room walkthrough, a demo account, or the participant describing their process from memory

conclusion.verdict: label the session `retrospective` and exclude it from behavioural claims in `themes`; re-book at the participant's own desk or screen, with their own data and their normal interruptions

branch.when: real work in the real place, but the plan is to read a scripted question list start to finish

conclusion.verdict: restore master/apprentice before running: participant works, researcher watches and asks in the moment, and record per session how context, partnership, interpretation and focus were met

branch.when: real work under master/apprentice, but only one participant is available in the role

conclusion.verdict: run it, but record what you see as a case with n=1 stated in the text — it is not a finding about the role until a second participant who never met the first does the same odd thing

branch.when: real ongoing work, master/apprentice agreed, and at least two participants per distinct role in the work practice

conclusion.verdict: apply the full methodology: four principles per session, separated observation and interpretation, in-session validation, captured artifacts, and themes cited across participants

branch.when: the sessions are done and the open question is how the notes become an artefact
branch.question: What do the rows look like as they are being written?

branch.when: rows read as single narrative sentences that mix what was seen with what it means

conclusion.verdict: split every row: literal `action` or verbatim `quote` in their own fields, `interpretation` in its own; a row with an interpretation and no observed action or quote is deleted, not softened

branch.when: interpretations were formed after the session and never spoken back to the participant

conclusion.verdict: mark those rows `validated=false` and bar them as sole support for a theme; the qualifier a participant would have supplied in the room is unrecoverable afterwards

branch.when: spreadsheets, checklists, sticky notes and chat threads are described in prose rather than captured

conclusion.verdict: go back for photos, screenshots or file references with consent and redaction noted — the columns of a private tracking spreadsheet are the data model the person actually needs, and prose collapses that to they keep some notes
